Whether the error is a correctable bias or a random floor that caps ranking, and how rank agreement holds over hundreds of molecules [s_ogbomo_db]. **Hypothesis.** Green–Kubo MD with one fixed force field has a chemistry-dependent error floor near 25 percent that more molecules cannot remove [s_ogbomo_res]. **If compute is the lever.** At 120 molecules, held-out viscosity error after bias correction falls below 15 percent and rank correlation with measurement exceeds 0.9 [s_ogbomo_res]. **If not.** Held-out viscosity error stays above 25 percent and rank correlation below 0.7 at every set size, capping candidate ranking [s_ogbomo_res]. **Test.** One LAMMPS LOPLS-AA Green–Kubo protocol at 40 °C, six five-nanosecond replicas per molecule, run on 8, 24, 48 then 120 molecules from the public 835-molecule reference set, scored only against measured viscosity and thermal conductivity [s_ogbomo_db]. *Compute axis.* Benchmark molecules scored against measured viscosity and thermal conductivity: 8–120 molecules, 4 levels. `card:hypothesis` PARTIAL · page: "Viscosity errors are small for the pure hydrocarbons with LOPLS, but this property is consistently under-predicted for the oxygen-containing molecules; the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved. Thermal conductivity is over-predicted for every molecule, by amounts that correlate with the density of aliphatic C–H bonds, compressing the reference range and misordering the fluids." · note: The source supports the qualitative claim of chemistry-dependent force-field errors in viscosity and thermal conductivity. It does not state a ~25% error floor (it reports viscosity errors from small up to 137% at 40 °C, with only four of eight molecules within 25%) and says nothing about more molecules being unable to remove the error; those parts are unsupported. - sample 1 · `card:left_open` PARTIAL · page: "We compile a database of approximately 4,700 critically evaluated reference values for the density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity of 835 unique organic molecules in the C10–C50 range." · note: The page supports only the scale claim ('hundreds of molecules', 835-molecule reference set). It does not state that whether the error is a correctable bias or a random floor, or rank agreement at that scale, is left open; the work reports that viscosity ranking is largely preserved among eight molecules, so the 'left open' framing is the plan's gap claim, not a finding on the page. - sample 1 · `card:limits` UNSUPPORTED · page: "Only molecules with a dynamic viscosity of approximately 1–50 mPa s at 40 °C were included, because this is the range accessible to equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) simulations." · note: The applicability claims ('only at 40 °C for pure liquids between 1 and 50 mPa·s, not blends or sold coolants') are factual claims about the evidence domain and the item cites no source, so they are UNSUPPORTED by the rule. (They do match the work's inclusion criteria on the page I fetched, but no source is cited here.) 'Cannot show ranking behaviour beyond 120 molecules' is plan scope and needs no source. - sample 1 · `src:s_ogbomo_res` PARTIAL · page: "Density is reproduced to within 4% for seven of the eight molecules at 40 °C. Viscosity errors are small for the pure hydrocarbons with LOPLS, but this property is consistently under-predicted for the oxygen-containing molecules; the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved. Thermal conductivity is over-predicted for every molecule, by amounts that correlate with the density of aliphatic C–H bonds, compressing the reference range and misordering the fluids." · note: The cited Spiral bitstream is the same article PDF (d6dd00260a.pdf) but returns unparseable PDF bytes; the identical text was confirmed in the published version of the same article. The quote supports the anchor tolerances and the qualitative error pattern, but not 'the predicted error floor' (no error floor is quantified) and only loosely the if_not expectation (it says viscosity ranking was largely preserved, and reports no 25%/0.7 thresholds). - sample 1 · `num:throughput_ns_day` PARTIAL · page: "JAC_PRODUCTION_NVE - 23,558 atoms PME 2fs ... 1 x A100 GPU: | ns/day = 611.08" · note: The quoted benchmark line appears on the Amber page for the stated setting (JAC_PRODUCTION_NVE, 23,558 atoms, PME, 2 fs, one A100), but the page states 611.08 ns/day, not 250. The 250 ns/day is a disclosed proxy (safety factor ~2.4 under the page figure, Amber pmemd.cuda protein-in-water rather than LAMMPS with stress-tensor accumulation), so the assumption is not contradicted, just not the page's number. · page value 611.08 - sample 2 · `card:hypothesis` PARTIAL · page: "The MD benchmark, using a Green–Kubo protocol with quantified trajectory-length convergence, shows that the accuracy of the LOPLS-AA force field is property- and chemistry dependent." · note: The page confirms Green–Kubo MD with one fixed force field (LOPLS-AA) and chemistry-dependent transport errors that persist at convergence (viscosity under-predicted 17–38% for esters and 26–57% for ethers; thermal conductivity over-predicted +7 to +96%). But no ~25% floor is stated anywhere, and the paper explicitly says that with only eight molecules these observations 'can only be used to identify plausible explanations, rather than establish firm conclusions' — so the 'near 25 percent' figure and 'more molecules cannot remove' are the plan's own extrapolation, not page content. - sample 2 · `card:limits` PARTIAL · page: "Only molecules with a dynamic viscosity of approximately 1–50 mPa·s at 40 °C were included, because this is the range accessible to equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) simulations." · note: The plan-scope limits (40 °C-only protocol; no ranking behaviour beyond 120 molecules) are the plan's own and need no source. The dataset-scope factual claims (pure liquids only, ~1–50 mPa·s, no blends) are correct per the Ogbomo paper but carry no source on this item; also note the published benchmark reported errors at both 40 °C and 100 °C, so 'only at 40 °C' holds for the plan's protocol (per test_summary), not for the prior paper. - sample 2 · `src:s_ogbomo_res` PARTIAL · page: "Density is reproduced to within 4% for seven of the eight molecules at 40 °C. Viscosity errors are small for the pure hydrocarbons with LOPLS, but this property is consistently under-predicted for the oxygen-containing molecules; the reference ranking of the fluids is nonetheless largely preserved. Thermal conductivity is over-predicted for every molecule, by amounts that correlate with the density of aliphatic C–H bonds, compressing the reference range and misordering the fluids." · note: The quote appears verbatim in the PDF served at this bitstream URL (conclusion section; confirmed via the indexed full text of this exact URL — a direct fetch returns a binary PDF that could not be text-extracted). It fully backs the anchor tolerances and qualitatively backs a chemistry-dependent, force-field-limited error floor, but the page nowhere states the ~25% floor or the if_not thresholds (>25% error, rank correlation <0.7), and for viscosity it reports the ranking 'largely preserved' while only thermal-conductivity ranking is misordered — so 'the predicted error floor and the if_not expectation' are only partly backed. **Critic.** - stakes 3 · `card:limits` "Shows transport-property error only at 40 °C for pure liquids between 1 and 50 mPa·s, not blends or sold coolants.
